name: Subscription compliance change monitor
demand: The regulatory trigger is real, but product demand is unproven. The government estimated 155 million active UK subscriptions and about £26bn in annual consumer spend in its 2 April 2026 response; those figures describe the consumer market, not software buyers: https://www.gov.uk/government/consultations/consultation-on-the-implementation-of-the-new-subscription-contracts-regime/outcome/government-response-to-consultation-on-the-implementation-of-the-new-subscription-contracts-regime-web-accessible-version. A 2023 impact assessment estimated 236,000 firms (4%) offered in-scope consumer subscriptions, based on a weighted survey of 244 firms and 2021 ONS business-population estimates; treat this as an old, modeled ceiling, not a current addressable customer count: https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/64464e6f529eda00123b02c4/annex_2-subscription_traps_impact_assessment.pdf. Public keyword-search volume, app installs, and user counts are unverified; Subnotice’s Shopify listing shows zero reviews, which does not establish its installs: https://apps.shopify.com/uk-subscription-guard.
prices: Advertised prices, not verified transactions: Subnotice is free for readiness scans and £15/month for paid features: https://app.subnotice.com/. Evidencee advertises free, £59, £149, and £449/month plans: https://evidencee.com/pricing; its terms leave company number and registered office as placeholders, so treat it cautiously: https://evidencee.com/terms. Compliance Radar advertises £500/month and £1,500/month for broader law-and-website monitoring: https://getcomplianceradar.com/pricing/. Upfront, an adjacent Shopify DMCC audit app, advertises $9.99/month: https://apps.shopify.com/upfront-uk-price-check.

revenue_proof.claim: No verifiable paid-customer count, sales receipt, or revenue event found in the reviewed public sources. Subnotice’s listing reports zero reviews, not zero users or revenue; competitor pages publish asking prices, not realized sales. Revenue proof is unverified.

copy_speed: Fast. Subnotice launched 22 June 2026 with a compliance score, pre-renewal notices, and audit evidence: https://apps.shopify.com/uk-subscription-guard. Upfront launched 1 September 2026 with a DMCC store audit, though its focus is hidden costs and discounts rather than subscription cancellation flows: https://apps.shopify.com/upfront-uk-price-check. Compliance Radar currently advertises ongoing law-and-website change monitoring and dated evidence, but its launch date is unverified: https://getcomplianceradar.com/how-it-works/. Evidencee advertises a direct DMCC compliance platform; its terms are marked effective September 2026, but its launch date is unverified: https://evidencee.com/terms.
platform_risk: Moderate to high if reliable checkout automation or Shopify integration is required. Shopify documents that subscription-contract access uses restricted scopes, including read_own_subscription_contracts, and requires approval; protected customer data has a separate approval process: https://shopify.dev/docs/api/usage/access-scopes. A public-page-only monitor avoids some integration dependence but cannot observe all login-gated or app-managed flows; Compliance Radar itself says its coverage is bounded to public pages: https://getcomplianceradar.com/faq/.
defensible_asset: Weak at launch. UK legislation and guidance are public, so summaries and a basic rules engine are readily reproducible: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2026/9780348287912/data.htm and https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/subscription-contracts. A useful asset could grow from tested mappings between legal duties and real checkout/cancellation steps, plus dated screenshots and a customer’s change history. Those would create some retention value, but no exclusive data or meaningful switching cost is demonstrated; this is an inference, not proven defensibility.
build_effort: Moderate for a narrow MVP that watches official sources and snapshots public URLs; high for dependable, low-false-positive testing of dynamic checkout and cancellation flows. Shopify’s restricted subscription scopes add integration friction: https://shopify.dev/docs/api/usage/access-scopes. Legal interpretation and false-positive review still need human judgment. No measured build effort, automation share, or operating hours exist; these are estimates, not verified performance.
channel: Use a product brand with inbound search content, a free public change log/checker, Shopify or WooCommerce listings, and opt-in partnerships or operator-community posts. This can reach remote subscription businesses without Ricardo’s face or personal brand. Avoid unsolicited electronic messages to sole traders and individuals: ICO guidance treats sole traders as individual subscribers and includes social-media DMs in electronic mail; consent or a qualifying soft opt-in is generally required: https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/.
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified. ≤5 hours/week seems plausible only for a narrow UK-law, public-page monitor with automated crawling and async support; legal triage, customer-specific audits, and platform integrations could push it above the limit.
desk_test: Within one day, manually produce an anonymized, source-linked sample report for a real public subscription flow and a one-page product offer. Test a £59/month price, matching Evidencee’s advertised Starter plan, through a permissioned operator community or opt-in partner channel; require a paid pilot commitment to count as evidence, not likes or stated interest. No coding or cold messages. If the channel produces no qualified traffic, the test is inconclusive rather than a demand failure.
red_flags: Conditional hold; do not build the full product yet. The regulations are still draft affirmative legislation laid on 19 October 2026, and the draft says they apply only to contracts entered after DMCC Act section 254 comes into force. Section 254 remains prospective in the latest point-in-time legislation, while the government’s April statement expected the regime in spring 2027; therefore 1 January 2027 is not a settled operative date: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukdsi/2026/9780348287912/introduction, https://www.legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2024/13/section/254/2026-09-30, https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-statements/detail/2026-04-13/hcws1498. The need may be a one-off compliance project rather than durable subscription monitoring. A direct-adjacent product launched in June, another DMCC audit app launched in September, and broader monitoring is already advertised. Competitor payment evidence remains unverified; Evidencee’s placeholder company details also weaken it as proof of a mature incumbent.
